thread.title: ETV: Tech Heavy Holdings With A High Yield - Eaton Vance Tax-Managed Buy-Write Opportunities Fund (NYSE:ETV)

author: Nick Ackerman
title: ETV: Tech Heavy Holdings With A High Yield - Eaton Vance Tax-Managed Buy-Write Opportunities Fund (NYSE:ETV)
text:
Eaton Vance Tax-Managed Buy-Write Opportunities Fund ( ETV ) might not be the best "value" closed-end fund at this time, with a slight premium of 1.41%, but the fund is still presenting an opportunity. The market had experienced a correction to end 2018 and many funds fell hard and sharp. ETV is no different as the market price went from $15.06 on 12/03/18 to the current $13.71 or an 8.9% drop as of 01/04/19. The NAV did not fair much better with a 12/03/18 price of $14.71 that is currently $13.52 or a drop of 8.08%. I believe this is giving an aggressive investor an opportunity to pick up a quality fund as it has pulled back significantly.
ETV is a sizable fund with total assets of $983 million according to CEFconnect. The larger size of the fund typically offers holders more liquidity as more shares tend to trade hands day-to-day. The fund also offers investors a reasonable expense ratio of 1.08%, this is what I would say is about average for a CEF. The fund doesn't utilize any leverage, they instead operate with an options strategy. Their latest Fact Sheet from Q3 2018 that they currently have 94% of their stock portfolio value through writing call options on indices.
Strategy And Return Of Capital They state their strategy as "the fund invests in a diversified portfolio of common stocks and writes call options on one or more U.S. indices on a substantial portion of the value of its common stock portfolio to generate current earnings from the option premiums." They also continue with "the fund evaluates returns on an after tax basis and seeks to minimize and defer federal income taxes incurred by shareholders in connection with their investment in the Fund." This strategy is easier for the managers to accomplish thanks to the fact that option income is paid out as return of capital (NYSE: ROC ).
In the case of ETV, taken from their 2017 Annual Report, the breakdown for the tax characteristics can be seen below.
Source - ETV Annual Report
Both 2017 and 2016 show a large portion of the distribution made up of ROC; additionally in 2016 long-term capital gains are present. There can be no guarantee going forward what the tax classifications will include but in the prior two years the fund has been able to deploy its strategy as stated.
Many investors who are new to CEFs are confused by ROC. ROC is not all created equal. Generally, as long as the fund's NAV is not being eroded or going downward year after year then the fund is paying out "good" ROC. The portion of the distribution that is considered ROC lowers an investors cost basis on the shares. This then defers tax obligations until an investor sells out of the fund, then the investor would be taxed at that point and it would be taxed as a capital gain. However, I am not a tax professional and every tax situation is different – please consult with a professional for individual tax advice.
Performance Source - CEFconnect
As you can see above the fund has not been immune to the price drop that the whole market has experienced. The prior drops in this fund also appear to have been attractive buying points for ETV. This time I believe is no different. The market price of the fund is currently $13.71, with a NAV price of $13.52; giving the fund a slight premium of 1.41%.
Source - Fund Website
Typically I wouldn't want to be purchasing a fund at any premium but it has been relatively rare in the last 5 years that this fund traded at a discount, it hasn't seen a significant discount since the beginning of 2014.
Source - CEFconnect
While the S&P 500 dropped more than 6% in 2018, ETV had performed slightly better. The fund experienced a market decline of 4.05%, with a lesser decline on a NAV basis of 2.62%.
Source - CEFconnect
Holdings While every stock appeared to fall significantly at the end of 2018, tech companies fell harder. This is no surprise as tech is famous for reacting even more volatile than other sectors. This tends to happen because when the economy is doing very well – tech companies tend to rise sharply, leading to further and faster declines when there are fears of growth in the global economy.
Source - Fund Website
The top holdings, especially the top 3, have a high percentage of total assets tied up. In particular, Apple ( AAPL ) has a significant 7.23% of total assets. For those that may live under a rock, Apple has started out 2019 on somewhat of a sour note. The stock dropped on January 3rd; from a closing price of $157.92 on January 2nd, to a closing price on January 3rd of $142.19.
AAPL 5 Day Returns (Daily) data by YCharts
This drop caused ETV to drop as well, just as both had been bouncing back from the correction. The reasoning behind the Apple drop was Tim Cook sending a letter to shareholders warning that revenue was going to be below expectations. The company's shares did slightly recover the very next day, though this was due partly to the overall market rallying on January 4th too. Apple's revenue is still tied significantly to iPhone sales, as iPhones make up ~60% of Apple's revenue . Though the company has for several years been increasing its dividend, and I believe this is a good sign that the management is confident they can continue to grow the company – not just relying on the iPhone alone. Apple's dividend info can be summed up below.
Source - Seeking Alpha
I wouldn't normally focus so heavily on just one holding but with the significant position of 7.23% in the top spot, it is definitely important to keep an eye on what Apple is doing.
Microsoft ( MSFT ) is also a significant position, but I personally view Apple with more uncertainty than Microsoft. Microsoft has been able to diversify its products and services better and find attractive growth in cloud services. Their cloud service named "Azure" had revenue growth of 76% in their Q1 October 24, 2018 earnings release . Their dividend growth has also been more impressive than Apple's.
Source - Seeking Alpha
ETV being significantly tied to the tech sector should give more conservative investors a pause though. This fund will make volatile moves when the broader market is going up or down. With this kind of volatility their option strategy can do little to help the downside, the real benefit of their option strategy appears to be increasing income potential and the fact a large chunk consists of tax-deferred ROC.
Distribution The current distribution is a very attractive 9.70% on the market price, with a NAV yield of 9.83%. The higher NAV yield is due to the fund trading at a slight premium. Even more appealing is the fact that the fund pays on a monthly schedule, at a rate of $0.1108. This same monthly distribution has been in place since beginning the monthly schedule in 2013. Prior to 2013 the fund paid out a quarterly distribution at a rate of $0.3323 (the equivalent of $0.1108 monthly), that rate had been maintained since December of 2010. That is when one of the two distribution cuts in the fund's history happened.
Source - CEFconnect
It should be noted though, that it appears Eaton Vance is starting to make decisions on their distributions with the latest market correction. Two funds from Eaton Vance have already announced distribution cuts, although two other funds have announced distribution increases.
Source - Seeking Alpha
The fund that is of particular interest is Eaton Vance Tax-Managed Global Buy-Write Opportunities Fund ( ETW ). That cut is significant as both ETV and ETW are very similar, the difference being ETW having a global focus. I believe that with the global focus the fund has under-performed significantly over the same time period as ETV and that is what lead Eaton Vance to make the cut.
ETV All Time Total Returns (Daily) data by YCharts
This might present investors that are looking for an opportunity to gain some exposure to global securities an opportunity. ETW has now fallen quite significantly after the cut was announced on January 2nd, and the fund is showing a discount of 3.97%.
ETW Price data by YCharts
ETW did also suffer because of holding Apple as their second largest position too, at about 4.12% as of November 30, 2018. Their top holding is Microsoft at 4.22%, along with all the big tech names and finally a couple companies that are located outside the U.S.
Source - Fund Website
I personally view ETV as a better option though at this time. With uncertainty going into 2019, I believe the U.S. market will be relatively more sheltered than funds that operate with a global tilt should we continue where we left off in 2018.
Conclusion ETV is presenting a great opportunity for investors that are betting on a strong market for 2019. The fact that the fund pays out an almost 10% distribution also means that investors are being paid generously to be patient for this fund to turn around. However, ETV isn't for investors that have a pessimistic view for 2019, as there could be much more pain ahead for a fund with such high exposure to the tech sector. With that knowledge, I purchased some additional shares on January 4th myself.
Disclosure: I am/we are long ETV, MSFT. I wrote this article myself, and it expresses my own opinions. I am not receiving compensation for it (other than from Seeking Alpha). I have no business relationship with any company whose stock is mentioned in this article.
